correctness.rationale: The Birkhoff--von Neumann theorem identifies the convex image with the hull of its integer permutation X-rays. For noncentral images, mass \(k\) and maximum occupancy \(k-1\) imply \(\|h\|_2^2\le(k-1)^2+1\). Nonnegative inner products then bound every noncentral pair below the claimed diameter. Central-to-image equality forces occupancy \(k-1\) on an off-central anti-diagonal; the row/column constraint gives exactly two images. Strict convexity rules out additional diametral points in the full polytope. For nonmaximal pairs with the central image, the extra \(k-2\) occupancy bound gives the sharp second distance, with an explicit permutation witness. The low-rank exceptions are checked. A reproducible exact-integer verifier passed 694526 assertions; unrestricted quantifiers rest on the written proof.

value.rationale: This is a complete natural infinite-family metric classification of an image whose facets grow superpolynomially in the matrix order. It determines every extreme distance segment (only one/two pairs), and a sharp second-highest distance with an explicit witness, rather than just substituting into a known norm formula. The gap \(2(k-3)\) is a structural quantitative separation for discrete anti-diagonal tomographic configurations; the same vectors encode distributions of a sum under arbitrary couplings of finite uniform marginals. The result distinguishes the projected metric sharply from the familiar Frobenius metric on the Birkhoff polytope. It neither relies on a narrow arbitrary parameter slice nor claims an unsupported external application.
